# Wavelet — product reference

Wavelet is a music recognition quiz played in a browser. The name is pronounced "wave-let". Its tagline is "Little clips. Big music energy." Previous interfaces used Vinyl Rush and 365 branding; Wavelet is the current product identity.

## Playing

Choose a challenge: Track ID asks for the song title; Artist Call asks who performs it; Sonic Genre asks for the genre. Year mode stays hidden. Choose Chill, Club, or Master difficulty. Select a music crate from genres, an exclusive artist filter, or a general catalog search. Clip lengths are 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Sets request 5, 10, or 15 songs. Artist crates contain only the selected artist’s songs and may be shorter; they never borrow unrelated tracks. Four-choice and self-scored reveal modes are available in round setup. Correct answers earn score, experience, and coins. Quests, badges, per-mode statistics, and progression are in the player profile.

## Studio

The title header shows the Wavelet identity, player profile, and Settings. Settings holds the master volume, mute control, sound effects, haptics, Daylight, After hours, or device-following appearance, motion preference, compact canvas, companion selection, backstage dance video, music crate connection, installation guidance, and keyboard help. Settings persist locally on the current browser. Reduced motion follows the device preference by default and can be selected explicitly. It reduces interface movement, decorative 3D motion, and celebratory particles, and pauses the dance video. Music clips remain playable.

## Keyboard

With the page focused and no modal open: Space or Enter starts a game from setup, P or Escape pauses or resumes, M mutes all audio, T changes appearance, and H toggles game controls during play. Native controls and dialog inputs retain their own keyboard behavior.

## Music and accounts

Online solo uses commercial previews from the iTunes catalog in the South African storefront, with real artist search and direct streaming from Apple’s preview CDN. Availability, regions, and browser policies can affect playback. Failed previews report an error without substituting audio. Choose Offline originals for 24 browser-generated Wavelet demos. Shared challenges and multiplayer use these originals. Music-account OAuth, personal library syncing and full-song playback are not connected. Google sign-in optionally synchronizes player progression; guest play is supported.

## Platform

Wavelet is a responsive Next.js application with a Three.js vinyl studio and animated topography, shadcn/ui controls, Phosphor icons, React Bits interactions, and Web Audio effects. It can be installed as a progressive web app on supported browsers. After the first successful production visit, the app shell, catalog metadata and UI sounds can be cached for offline use. Commercial audio is not cached by the service worker and requires a connection; Offline originals work without streaming. Updates are applied from Settings between sets. Authentication callbacks and private APIs bypass the cache. The app follows system appearance before the first paint and supports safe areas, fullscreen, and native media controls where available. Haptic feedback depends on browser and device support. Browser JavaScript, audio support, and WebGL are recommended. The public entry point is /. The canonical LLM overview is /llms.txt, with /llm.txt as a discoverability alias.
